context.zh: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」
context.idiomatic: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”
context.literal: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness’s inspired plans flashed forth like lightning and swept away the vile rebels. You should report the victory in an open dispatch, inflating the tally of severed heads to reassure people far and near.”

context.zh: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」
context.idiomatic: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
context.literal: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”

context.zh: 其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。」
context.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Wei Hua, the right vice-director, told Murong Zhu, governor of Henan, “The crown prince truly is respectful and kind. That is a blessing for the state.”
context.literal: His right vice-director Wei Hua heard it and said to Henan Grand Administrator Murong Zhu, "The crown prince truly has the virtue of reverence and kindness—blessing for the altars."

context.zh: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。
context.idiomatic: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.
context.literal: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

context.zh: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。

context.literal: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

context.zh: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。
context.idiomatic: When Yao Hong claimed the imperial throne, he entrusted Yao Shao with military command. Moved by this, Shao pledged himself to Hong and remained loyal to the end.
context.literal: When he presumptuously mounted the throne, he entrusted Shao with military authority; Shao was also moved and returned sincerity, and in the end kept his loyal fierceness.

context.zh: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。
context.idiomatic: After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.
context.literal: After burial, he then personally attended to myriad government; inner and outer hundred officials were raised one rank in position; he ordered civil and military each to exhaust straight speech—where government had what was not convenient to the time, or affairs that could add lustre to the ancestral temple, speak to the utmost without hiding.

context.zh: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。
context.idiomatic: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.
context.literal: At this point, Qiang chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return; he sent General Who Pacifies Yao Zan to campaign against him.

context.zh: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。
context.idiomatic: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.
context.literal: At this point, Qiang chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return; he sent General Who Pacifies Yao Zan to campaign against him.

context.zh: 姚宣時鎮李閏，未知雍敗，遣部將姚佛生等來衛長安。
context.idiomatic: Yao Xuan was then garrisoning Lirun and had not yet learned that Mao Yong had been defeated, so he sent his subordinate commander Yao Fosheng and others to defend Chang'an.
context.literal: Yao Xuan then garrisoned Li-run, not yet knowing of Yong's defeat, sent subordinate generals Yao Fosheng and others to come guard Chang'an.

context.zh: 宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。
context.idiomatic: Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.
context.literal: Xuan then led thirty-eight thousand households, abandoned Li-run, and went south to hold Xingwang.

context.zh: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。
context.idiomatic: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.
context.literal: Once Xuan had moved south, the various Qiang occupied Li-run in revolt; Shao advanced and campaigned, defeated them.

context.zh: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。
context.idiomatic: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.
context.literal: Once Xuan had moved south, the various Qiang occupied Li-run in revolt; Shao advanced and campaigned, defeated them.

context.zh: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。
context.idiomatic: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.
context.literal: Xuan went to Shao to confess guilt; Shao in anger killed him.

context.zh: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。
context.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.
context.literal: At first, while Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Yao Fosheng to instruct Xuan; Fosheng then endorsed Xuan's plan.

context.zh: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。
context.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.
context.literal: At first, while Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Yao Fosheng to instruct Xuan; Fosheng then endorsed Xuan's plan.

context.zh: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」
context.idiomatic: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”
context.literal: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as viscounts and barons in the five grades of nobility. Yao Zan remonstrated, “The Eastern Palace’s civil and military officers naturally owe it faithful loyalty. They have yet to show conspicuous merit. Why should they receive so many grants of fiefs?”

context.zh: 元子遭家不造，與宮臣同此百憂，獨享其福，得不愧於心乎！」
context.idiomatic: I, Yuanzi, have seen my house struck by misfortune. My palace officers shared all these troubles with me. Could I enjoy the good fortune alone without feeling ashamed?”
context.literal: Yuanzi meets the house in misfortune, sharing every worry with palace officials—how could he alone enjoy the blessing without shame in heart!"

context.zh: 并州、定陽、貳城胡數萬落叛泓，入於平陽，攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡，推匈奴曹弘為大單于，所在殘掠。
context.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.
context.literal: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.

context.zh: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘，戰於平陽，大破之，執弘，送于長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。
context.idiomatic: Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East, marched from Puban against Cao Hong, routed him at Pingyang, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. Yi resettled fifteen thousand leading households in Yongzhou.
context.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi set out from Puban against Cao Hong. He fought at Pingyang, routed Hong, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. He transferred fifteen thousand of their leading households to Yongzhou.

context.zh: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘，戰於平陽，大破之，執弘，送于長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。

context.zh: 泓遣後將軍姚平救之，盛引退。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to relieve Qinzhou, and Yang Sheng withdrew.
context.literal: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to rescue him; Sheng withdrew.

context.zh: 秦州地震者三十二，殷殷有聲者八，山崩舍壞，咸以為不祥。
context.idiomatic: Qinzhou suffered thirty-two earthquakes, eight accompanied by rumbling. Mountains collapsed and houses fell. Everyone took these as ill omens.
context.literal: In Qinzhou there were thirty-two earthquakes with rumbling sound in eight cases; mountains collapsed and houses ruined—all thought it inauspicious.

context.zh: 赫連勃勃攻陷陰密，執秦州刺史姚軍都，坑將士五千餘人。
context.idiomatic: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, inspector of Qinzhou, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and men.
context.literal: Helian Bobo attacked and took Yinmi, seized Qinzhou Inspector Yao Jundu, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and soldiers.

context.zh: 勃勃既克陰密，進兵侵雍，嶺北雜戶悉奔五將山。
context.idiomatic: After taking Yinmi, Bobo advanced on Yong. The mixed households north of the ridge all fled to Five Generals Mountain.
context.literal: Once Bobo had taken Yinmi, he advanced troops to invade Yong; north-of-the-ridge miscellaneous households all fled to Five-General Mountain.

context.zh: 征北姚恢棄安定，率戶五千奔新平，安定人胡儼、華韜等率眾距恢，恢單騎歸長安。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, abandoned Anding and fled toward Xinping with five thousand households. Hu Yan, Hua Tao and others from Anding led their followers against him, and Hui returned to Chang’an alone on horseback.
context.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui abandoned Anding, led five thousand households to flee to Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao led hosts to block Hui; Hui alone on horseback returned to Chang'an.

context.zh: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定，胡儼閉門距之，殺鮮卑數千人，據安定以降。
context.idiomatic: Shao’s army halted at Hengshui. Bobo fell back toward Anding, hoping to hold it, but Hu Yan shut the gates against him, killed several thousand Xianbei and surrendered Anding to Qin.
context.literal: The army halted at Hengshui; Bobo withdrew to guard Anding; Hu Yan closed the gate to block him, killed several thousand Xianbei, and occupied Anding to surrender.

context.zh: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定，胡儼閉門距之，殺鮮卑數千人，據安定以降。

context.zh: 紹進兵躡勃勃，戰於馬鞍阪，敗之，追至朝那，不及而還。
context.idiomatic: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.
context.literal: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.

context.zh: 平陽氐苟渴聚眾千餘，據五丈原以叛，遣鎮遠姚萬、恢武姚難討之，為渴所敗。
context.idiomatic: Gou Ke, a Di man of Pingyang, gathered more than a thousand men and occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt. Yao Hong sent Yao Wan, General Who Guards the Distant Lands, and Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, against him. Gou Ke defeated them.
context.literal: Pingyang Di Gou Ke gathered more than a thousand, occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt; he sent General Who Guards the Distance Yao Wan and General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to campaign against him, and they were defeated by Ke.

context.zh: 平陽氐苟渴聚眾千餘，據五丈原以叛，遣鎮遠姚萬、恢武姚難討之，為渴所敗。

context.literal: Pingyang Di Gou Ke gathered more than a thousand, occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt; he sent General Who Guards the Distance Yao Wan and General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to campaign against him, and they were defeated by Ke.

context.zh: 泓使輔國斂曼嵬、前將軍姚光兒討楊倦于陳倉，倦奔于散關。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.
context.literal: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.

context.zh: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡入自淮、肥，攻漆丘、項城，將軍沈林子自汴入河，攻倉垣。
context.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin’s grand commandant Liu Yu led a great army against Yao Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen’e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi entered the Yellow River from the Bian and attacked Cangyuan.
context.literal: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.

context.zh: 泓將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，王師遂入潁口，所至多降服。
context.idiomatic: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.
context.literal: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.

context.zh: 姚紹聞王師之至，還長安，言於泓曰：「晉師已過許昌，豫州、安定孤遠，卒難救衛，宜遷諸鎮戶內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，足以橫行天下。
context.idiomatic: Hearing that the Jin army had arrived, Yao Shao returned to Chang’an and told Hong, “Jin has already passed Xuchang. Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and distant. It would be hard to relieve them at short notice. Move the garrison households inward to strengthen the capital region. We could raise a hundred thousand picked troops, enough to range unchallenged throughout the realm.
context.literal: When Yao Shao heard the royal army had arrived, he returned to Chang'an and said to Hong, "The Jin army has passed Xuchang; Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and far; in the end hard to rescue—it is fitting to move the garrison households inward to fill the capital region; you can obtain crack troops of one hundred thousand, enough to range across the realm.

context.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「齊公恢于廣平之難有忠勳于陛下，自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞以答其意。
context.idiomatic: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since you took the throne, he has received no special reward in recognition of his devotion.
context.literal: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since Your Majesty rose like a dragon and succeeded to the throne, no special reward has acknowledged Hui’s devotion.

context.zh: 泓遣越騎校尉閻生率騎三千以赴之，武衛姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣征東、并州牧姚懿南屯陝津為之聲援。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue and the Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. He also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.
context.literal: Hong sent Colonel of Agile Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horse to hurry there, Martial Guard Yao Yinan leading ten thousand foot soldiers to assist in guarding Luoyang, and also sent General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Bingzhou Yao Yi to camp south at Shan ford as sounding support.

context.zh: 金墉既固，師無損敗，吳寇終不敢越金墉而西。
context.idiomatic: With Jinyong strongly held and our army intact, the invaders from Wu will never dare pass the fortress and march west.
context.literal: Once Metal Rampart is firm, the army suffers no defeat, and the Wu bandits in the end dare not cross Metal Rampart westward.

context.zh: 洸從之，乃遣玄率精兵千餘南守柏穀塢，廣武石無諱東戍鞏城，以距王師。
context.idiomatic: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.
context.literal: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.

context.zh: 玄與晉將毛德祖戰于柏穀，以眾寡而敗，被瘡十餘，據地大呼，玄司馬騫鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾瘡已重，君宜速去。」
context.idiomatic: At Baigu, Zhao Xuan fought the Jin general Mao Dezu and was defeated by superior numbers. He received more than ten wounds and cried out from the ground. His major, Qian Jian, braved the blades to hold him in his arms and wept. Xuan said, “My wounds are grave. You must leave at once.”
context.literal: Xuan fought Jin general Mao Dezu at Baigu; because few against many he was defeated, received more than ten wounds, clutched the ground and shouted; Xuan's Major Qian Jian braved blades, embraced Xuan and wept; Xuan said, "My wounds are already heavy—you ought quickly to depart."

context.zh: 懿納之，乃引兵至陝津，散谷以賜河北夷夏，欲虛損國儲，招引和戎諸羌，樹已私惠。
context.idiomatic: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.
context.literal: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

context.zh: 懿納之，乃引兵至陝津，散谷以賜河北夷夏，欲虛損國儲，招引和戎諸羌，樹已私惠。
context.idiomatic: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.
context.literal: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

context.zh: 懿左常侍張敞、侍郎左雅固諫懿曰：「殿下以母弟之親，居分陝之重，安危休戚，與國共之。
context.idiomatic: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.
context.literal: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.

context.zh: 今吳寇內侵，四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危有同累卵，正是諸侯勤王之日。
context.idiomatic: The Wu invaders are now inside, four provinces have fallen, western raiders disturb the border, and Qin and Liang have been overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is the hour for the lords to rally to the throne.
context.literal: Now the Wu bandit invades within, four provinces have toppled, western raiders disturb the border, Qin and Liang are overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is exactly the day when lords should aid the king.

context.zh: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至者，臣當遣懿率河東見兵共平吳寇。
context.idiomatic: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.

context.zh: 於是遣姚贊及冠軍司馬國璠、建義蛇玄屯陝津，武衛姚驢屯潼關。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.
context.literal: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.

context.zh: 懿遂舉兵僭號，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡穀以給鎮人。
context.idiomatic: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.
context.literal: Yi thereupon raised troops and presumptuously assumed title, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wished to transport Xiongnu Fort grain to supply the garrison men.

context.zh: 懿又遣驍騎王國率甲士數百攻成都，成都擒國，囚之，遣讓懿曰：「明公以母弟之親，受推轂之寄，今社稷之危若綴旒然，宜恭恪憂勤，匡輔王室。
context.idiomatic: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
context.literal: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.

context.zh: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！
context.idiomatic: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?
context.literal: Yet you harbor treachery and plot danger to the ancestral temple—can the spirits of the three ancestors rest easy with you!

context.zh: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！
context.idiomatic: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?
context.literal: Yet you harbor treachery and plot danger to the ancestral temple—can the spirits of the three ancestors rest easy with you!

context.zh: 臨晉數千戶叛應懿。
context.idiomatic: Several thousand households in Linjin rose in support of Yao Yi.
context.literal: Several thousand households of Linjin rebelled to answer Yi.

context.zh: 姚紹濟自薄津，擊臨晉叛戶，大破之，懿等震懼。
context.idiomatic: Yao Shao crossed at Bo Ford and routed the rebel households of Linjin. Yao Yi and his followers were shaken with fear.
context.literal: Yao Shao crossed from Bo ford, struck the Linjin rebel households, greatly defeated them; Yi and others were shaken with fear.

context.zh: 鎮人安定郭純、王奴等率眾圍懿。
context.idiomatic: Guo Chun, Wang Nu and other garrison men from Anding led their followers in surrounding Yao Yi.
context.literal: Garrison men of Anding Guo Chun and Wang Nu and others led hosts to surround Yi.

context.zh: 泓以內外離叛，王師漸逼，歲旦朝群臣於其前殿，淒然流涕，群臣皆泣。
context.idiomatic: With defections at home and abroad and the Jin army drawing nearer, Yao Hong received his ministers in the front hall on New Year’s morning. He shed tears of grief, and the ministers all wept.
context.literal: Because inner and outer split in rebellion and the royal army pressed gradually, on New Year's dawn Hong met the host of ministers in his front hall, wept dismally; the host of ministers all wept.

context.zh: 時征北姚恢率安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚燒室宇，以車為方陣，自北雍州趣長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, burned the houses and led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households toward Chang’an from North Yongzhou, forming his wagons into a square. He styled himself grand commander-in-chief and Great General Who Establishes Righteousness and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies declaring his intent to rid the ruler’s side of evil men.
context.literal: At the time General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households, burned houses, formed a chariot square, went from North Yongzhou toward Chang'an, styled himself grand commander-in-chief and great general who establishes righteousness, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wishing to remove evil beside the ruler.

context.zh: 時征北姚恢率安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚燒室宇，以車為方陣，自北雍州趣長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡。

context.zh: 揚威姜紀率眾奔之。
context.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, General Who Displays Might, led his men to join Hui.
context.literal: General Who Displays Might Jiang Ji led hosts to join him.

context.zh: 鎮西姚諶為恢所敗，恢軍勢彌盛，長安大震。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hui defeated Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West. Hui’s army gathered still greater strength, and Chang’an was badly shaken.
context.literal: General Who Guards the West Yao Chen was defeated by Hui; Hui's army momentum grew ever stronger; Chang'an was greatly shaken.

context.zh: 扶風太守姚雋、安夷護軍姚墨蠡、建威姚娥都、揚威彭蠔皆懼而降恢。
context.idiomatic: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
context.literal: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.

context.zh: 恢舅苟和時為立節將軍，守忠不貳，泓召而謂之曰：「眾人咸懷去就，卿何能自安邪？」
context.idiomatic: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
context.literal: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”

context.zh: 恢舅苟和時為立節將軍，守忠不貳，泓召而謂之曰：「眾人咸懷去就，卿何能自安邪？」
context.idiomatic: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
context.literal: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”

context.zh: 和曰：「若天縱妖賊，得肆其逆節者，舅甥之理，不待賓士而加親。
context.idiomatic: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
context.literal: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.

context.zh: 姚紹率輕騎先赴難，使姚洽、司馬國璠將步卒三萬赴長安。
context.idiomatic: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
context.literal: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.

context.zh: 姚贊聞恢漸逼，留甯朔尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，率諸軍還長安。
context.idiomatic: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
context.literal: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.

context.zh: 姚贊聞恢漸逼，留甯朔尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，率諸軍還長安。
context.idiomatic: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
context.literal: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.

context.zh: 道濟白陝北渡，攻蒲阪，使將軍苟卓攻匈奴堡，為泓甯東姚成都所敗。
context.idiomatic: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.
context.literal: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.

context.zh: 於是遣紹率武衛姚鸞等步騎五萬，距王師於潼關。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Shao, with Martial Guard commander Yao Luan and others, at the head of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose the Jin army at Tong Pass.
context.literal: Thereupon he sent Shao leading Martial Guard Yao Luan and others, fifty thousand foot and horse, to block the royal army at Tong Pass.

context.zh: 於是遣紹率武衛姚鸞等步騎五萬，距王師於潼關。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Shao, with Martial Guard commander Yao Luan and others, at the head of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose the Jin army at Tong Pass.
context.literal: Thereupon he sent Shao leading Martial Guard Yao Luan and others, fifty thousand foot and horse, to block the royal army at Tong Pass.

context.zh: 姚贊率禁兵七千，自渭北而東，進據蒲津。
context.idiomatic: Yao Zan led seven thousand palace guards east from north of the Wei River and advanced to occupy Pu Ford.
context.literal: Yao Zan led seven thousand household troops from north of the Wei eastward and advanced to occupy Pu ford.

context.zh: 劉裕使沈田子及傅弘之率眾萬餘人入上洛，所在多委城鎮奔長安。
context.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo with more than ten thousand men. In many places people abandoned their cities and garrisons and fled to Chang’an.
context.literal: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi leading more than ten thousand to enter Shangluo; place after place mostly abandoned cities and towns and fled to Chang'an.

context.zh: 姚鸞遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南，為琰所獲，送之劉裕。
context.idiomatic: Yao Luan sent his general Yin Ya against Xu Yan, Tan Daoji’s major, south of Tong Pass. Xu Yan captured Yin Ya and sent him to Liu Yu.
context.literal: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya against Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; Ya was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.

context.zh: 雅曰：「前活本在望外，今死寧不甘心。
context.idiomatic: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?
context.literal: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?

context.zh: 明公將以大義平天下，豈可使秦無守信之臣乎！」
context.idiomatic: You intend to pacify the realm through great righteousness. How can you deny Qin a minister who keeps faith with his ruler?”
context.literal: The enlightened lord will use great righteousness to pacify the realm—how can you make Qin lack a faithful subject!"

context.zh: 泓遣給事黃門侍郎姚和都屯于堯柳，以備田子。
context.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.
context.literal: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.

context.zh: 姚贊屯於河上，遣恢武姚難運蒲阪穀以給其軍，至香城，為王師所敗。
context.idiomatic: Yao Zan camped on the Yellow River and sent Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, to bring grain from Puban to supply his army. When Nan reached Xiangcheng, the Jin army defeated him.
context.literal: Yao Zan camped on the river, sent General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to transport Puban grain to supply the army; reaching Xiangcheng, he was defeated by the royal army.

context.zh: 時泓遣姚諶守堯柳，姚和都討薛帛於河東，聞王師要難，乃兼道赴救，未至而難敗，固破裕裨將于河曲，遂屯蒲阪。
context.idiomatic: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.
context.literal: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.

context.zh: 紹遣左長史姚洽及姚墨蠡等率騎三千屯于河北之九原，欲絕道濟諸縣租輸。
context.idiomatic: Yao Shao sent his left chief clerk Yao Qia, Yao Moli and others with three thousand cavalry to camp at Jiuyuan north of the Yellow River. He meant to cut off the tax-grain shipments that the counties were sending Tan Daoji.
context.literal: Shao sent left chief clerk Yao Qia and Yao Moli and others leading three thousand horse to camp at Jiuyuan north of the He, wishing to cut off Daoji's county rent convoys.

context.zh: 今兵眾單弱，而遠在河外，雖明公神武，然鞭短勢殊，恐無所及。」
context.idiomatic: Our troops are few and weak, far away beyond the Yellow River. For all your military prowess, my lord, your whip is short and the forces unequal. I fear you will be unable to reach us.”
context.literal: Now the troops are few and weak and far beyond the river—though the enlightened lord is divinely martial, yet the whip is short and the power situation unequal—I fear there is no reaching them."

context.zh: 沈林子率眾八千，耍洽於河上，洽戰死，眾皆沒。
context.idiomatic: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.
context.literal: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.

context.zh: 泓以晉師之逼，遣使乞師于魏。
context.idiomatic: As the Jin army pressed closer, Yao Hong sent envoys to Wei to ask for troops.
context.literal: Because the Jin army pressed, Hong sent envoys begging troops from Wei.

context.zh: 裕為田子所敗，泓退次於灞上，關中郡縣多潛通于王師。
context.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.
context.literal: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.

context.zh: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北，以攻蒲阪。
context.idiomatic: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.
context.literal: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.

context.zh: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬自秋社西渡渭，以逼難軍。
context.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
context.literal: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen’e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei and press Yao Nan’s army.

context.zh: 鎮東姚璞及姚和都擊敗猗之等於蒲阪，猗之遇害，超石棄其眾奔於潼關。
context.idiomatic: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.
context.literal: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.

context.zh: 鎮惡水陸兼進，追及姚難。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e advanced by water and by land and overtook Yao Nan.
context.literal: Zhen'e advanced by water and land together, caught up with Yao Nan.

context.zh: 鎮北姚彊率郡人數千，與姚難陣於涇上，以距鎮惡。
context.idiomatic: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.
context.literal: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.

context.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e sent Mao Dezu against Yao Qiang. Qiang’s force was routed, and Qiang died in battle. Yao Nan fled back to Chang’an.
context.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.

context.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。

context.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.

context.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
context.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

context.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。
context.idiomatic: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.
context.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.

context.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。
context.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.
context.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.

context.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。
context.idiomatic: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.
context.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

context.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。
context.idiomatic: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.
context.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

context.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

context.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。」
context.idiomatic: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”
context.literal: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”

context.zh: 泓將妻子詣壘門而降。
context.idiomatic: Hong took his wife and children to the gate of the Jin camp and surrendered.
context.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.

context.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。
context.idiomatic: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.
context.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.

context.zh: 史評
context.idiomatic: Historical Appraisal
context.literal: Historical Appraisal

context.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。
context.idiomatic: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
context.literal: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.

context.zh: 弋仲越自金方，言歸石氏，抗直詞於暴主，闡忠訓于危朝，貽厥之謀，在乎歸順，鳴哀之義，有足稱焉。
context.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
context.literal: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.

context.zh: 取汾、絳，陷許、洛，款僭燕而籓偽蜀，夷隴右而靜河西，俗阜年豐，遠安邇輯，雖楚莊、秦穆何以加焉！
context.idiomatic: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
context.literal: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo, won the submission of the usurping Yan regime and made the pretended regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those nearby were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

context.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！
context.idiomatic: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
context.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!

context.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！
context.idiomatic: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
context.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!

context.zh: 況乎偽境日侵，寧堪永貴之役！
context.idiomatic: How, then, could a realm whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the cost of building the Buddhist stupa at Yonggui?
context.literal: How much less could a usurping regime, its borders daily encroached upon, bear the labor of construction at Yonggui?

context.zh: 儲用殫竭，山林有稅，政荒威挫，職是之由，坐致淪胥，非天喪也。
context.idiomatic: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.
context.literal: Stores were exhausted, hills and forests taxed; government wild, awe broken—this is the reason; sitting to bring ruin—Heaven did not destroy them.

context.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；
context.idiomatic: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
context.literal: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.

context.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。
context.idiomatic: The wicked heir, at a loss for any plan, surrendered with the cord about his neck, like the Qin ruler at Zhidao.
context.literal: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.
